record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Where does Kakutani equivalence on ergodic measure-preserving transformations lie among analytic equivalence relations, and is it reducible to an S∞-action?

evidence.quote: Question 1.18. Where does the Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations sit among the analytic equivalence relations? Is it reducible to an S∞-action?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic probability space, and let $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ denote the Polish space of ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, equipped with the weak topology. Two transformations $T,S \in \mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$ are said to be Kakutani equivalent if there exist measurable sets $A \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $T$-sweeping out) and $B \subseteq X$ (positive measure, $S$-sweeping out) such that the induced transformations $T_A$ and $S_B$ are measure-theoretically isomorphic (equivalently, $T$ and $S$ have measurably isomorphic suspension flows up to a time change). This defines an analytic equivalence relation $E_K$ on $\mathrm{Erg}(X,\mu)$.

Recall the framework of Borel reducibility: for analytic equivalence relations $E$ on a Polish space $X$ and $F$ on a Polish space $Y$, one writes $E \leq_B F$ if there is a Borel function $f : X \to Y$ such that $x E x' \iff f(x) F f(x')$. An equivalence relation $E$ is said to be classifiable by an $S_\infty$-action (where $S_\infty$ is the Polish group of permutations of $\mathbb{N}$) if $E \leq_B F$ for some orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$ on a Polish space; equivalently, $E$ is Borel reducible to the isomorphism relation on countable structures in some countable language.

Determine the precise location of the Kakutani equivalence relation $E_K$ in the Borel-reducibility hierarchy of analytic equivalence relations. In particular, decide whether $E_K$ is Borel reducible to an orbit equivalence relation induced by a Borel action of $S_\infty$.
artifact.category_tag: Borel reducibility of equivalence relations in ergodic theory
artifact.status_search_result: Foreman, Gerber and Kunde proved that the Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of a standard non-atomic probability space is not a Borel set, ruling out classification by countable structures with Borel-computable invariants and showing non-reducibility to many classification problems. However, the precise location of $E_K$ among analytic equivalence relations and, in particular, whether it is Borel reducible to an $S_\infty$-orbit equivalence relation, does not appear to have been fully settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for the Kakutani equivalence relation
status_evidence.snippet: The Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformations of a standard non-atomic probability space is not a Borel set.
status_evidence.claim: It is known that the Kakutani equivalence relation is analytic but not Borel, so its complexity is strictly above Borel equivalence relations.

status_evidence.title: Anti-classification results for weakly mixing diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: The isomorphism relation as well as the Kakutani equivalence relation of weakly mixing invertible measure-preserving transformations are not Borel sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent anti-classification results extend non-Borelness of Kakutani equivalence to natural subclasses, but do not pinpoint its position among analytic equivalence relations nor determine reducibility to S∞-actions.
